channel.title: The Daily Boss
channel.description: Three minutes a day to put AI to work in your business. A daily brief from Miguel Carrasco.

item.title: Three times the output, none of the hours back
item.description:
Issue 019 · August 21, 2026
Three times the output, none of the hours back
The Big Story
 
Linear, the tracker a lot of software teams run their work through, published its own usage data this week, and one pair of numbers has been sitting with me since. Teams that connected an AI coding agent went from opening about 21 pull requests a week to about 65, roughly tripling the finished work going out the door. Teams that never connected one went from 8 to 10. If you wanted a clean advertisement for putting AI into your operation, there it is.
The rest of the report is where it gets honest. None of that output handed anybody their afternoon back. Time spent on the work already in the system held right where it was, and the AI work showed up as a new layer stacked on top, so total hours going into building things went up instead of down. Just under half of everything created in the tool now comes from agents rather than from people, and by the first week of August those two lines had nearly crossed.
The tools did exactly what they promised. Everything downstream of them stayed the same size.
What It Means For You
 
I did this to myself last year. I got a system running that could write a month of content in an afternoon, felt like a genius for about a day, then spent three weeks reading drafts to work out which ones were any good. The writing had never been what held me up. Deciding was, and I had just handed the machine the easy half.
Whatever you have automated, the work moved rather than vanished. It sits now in front of whoever approves, edits, answers, or signs off. If that person is you, and nobody gave you more hours, then your business got faster right up to your desk and stopped.
Quick Hits
 
–Microsoft patched a Copilot flaw on August 18 that let one malicious link quietly pull data out of a person's connected email, calendar, and Drive. The researchers who found it had reported it in December 2025.
–OpenAI started rolling out a teen version of ChatGPT on August 18 for ages 13 to 17, switched on by the system's own guess at a user's age rather than by any ID check.
–A security firm's AI agent found a command injection hole in one of Snowflake's public repositories, and the two companies are still arguing over whether an AI tool helped write the flawed code.
Try This Today
 
Pick one thing your AI has been producing more of, whether that is posts, proposals, replies, or listings. Count how many it made last week, then count how many actually went out the door. If those two numbers sit far apart, your next hour belongs to the gap between them rather than to generating anything else.
The Mindset
 
These reports all land the same way for me. The machine gets faster every quarter and the person in the chair does not. Building has always meant deciding what deserves to exist, and a model can draft a hundred versions of your offer before lunch while having no idea which one your customer needs to hear on a Tuesday when money is tight. That judgment does not scale, and I have stopped wishing it would.
Read this issue on the website →
If this email landed in spam or promotions, drag it to your inbox so tomorrow's issue lands where it belongs.
Keep building,
Miguel
